subject: SLA template: regional latency carve-out and escalating monthly credit proposal
messages:
From: Kira Johnson <kira@stratusai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@stratusai.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA discussion — regional latency carve-out

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we discussed, StratusAI runs bursty inference for video analytics during business hours in us-west. We need an SLA that recognizes regional traffic peaks and preserves a 99.95% uptime baseline nationally while allowing a limited regional carve-out for latency during predictable burst windows.

Specifically: can Redwood accept a policy that: 1) guarantees 99.95% uptime on a monthly national basis; 2) defines a regional latency SLO (p99 tail at <1200ms) that may be relaxed to p99 <2000ms for up to 4 predefined burst hours per week in a single region without counting as downtime; and 3) uses an escalating credit schedule tied to effective national uptime and regional latency breaches (not a flat monthly credit).

I've attached our proposed redline (Stratus_SLA_Redline_v3.pdf) and a simple spreadsheet showing how we expect credits to accrue depending on severity and frequency (uptime_credit_calculator.xlsx).

Can you circulate this to your pricing and legal team and let us know which parts are acceptable in principle? We're trying to avoid a one-size-fits-all credit table — we want credits that scale with the operational impact.

Best,
Kira
Director of Ops, StratusAI

---
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Kira Johnson <kira@stratusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA discussion — regional latency carve-out

Kira — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Laura (legal).

Initial thoughts:
- National uptime baseline at 99.95% is within our usual templates for reserved/dedicated capacity.
- Regional latency carve-outs are reasonable, but we need to define the trigger windows and an objective way to label an event as a "burst hour" so it cannot be overused.
- Escalating credits are doable — we typically prefer a combination of a baseline monthly credit + incremental credits for repeat or severe incidents. Your spreadsheet helps; we'll model a version that preserves predictable economics for both sides.

Ben/Laura — can you review the redline and the proposed credit math this week? Kira, we may have a short set of clarifying questions once Ben has run the numbers.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Kira Johnson <kira@stratusai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA discussion — regional latency carve-out

Kira / Alex — reviewed the attachments. A few practical constraints from pricing side:

1) Predictability: our finance team wants an upper bound on monthly credits as a function of committed spend. We can do escalating credits, but we'd cap total credits at a percent of monthly committed fees (typical cap is 25%).
2) Burst hours: suggest you predefine up to 8 weekly burst windows (each up to 1 hour) per region in your MAT (mutual action plan). Any additional ad-hoc burst allowances will consume a predefined burst budget.
3) Severity bands: propose a three-tier model:
   - Tier A: national downtime below 99.95% => baseline credit = 5% monthly fee per 0.01% below 99.95% (cumulative up to cap)
   - Tier B: regional latency breach outside allowed burst hours => fixed credit per incident (calculated as X% of daily bill)
   - Tier C: repeated regional latency breaches within a 30-day window => multiplier applies to Tier B credits (2x for 2nd-3rd incident, 3x beyond)
I modeled these in the spreadsheet and left comments.

Open questions: what do you consider an "incident" for latency (single sustained 5+ minute period above p99 threshold?), and do you want a mechanism for waiving credits for verified customer-side misconfigurations?

Ben
Director, Pricing Operations, Redwood Inference

---
From: Kira Johnson <kira@stratusai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@stratusai.com
Date: 2027-05-04T07:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA discussion — regional latency carve-out

Ben — thanks, this is helpful. On your questions:
- Incident definition: we proposed a continuous 10-minute window above the p99 threshold for latency incidents in the redline, but can shift to 5 minutes if you need stricter detection. The key is that brief spikes should not be classified as incidents unless they persist.
- Customer-side misconfigurations: yes, we expect a standard carve-out for customer configuration/traffic spikes outside our control, but StratusAI is asking for a transparent diagnostics process (structured post-incident review) rather than unilateral credit denials.

We can accept predefined weekly burst windows, but prefer limiting those to 4 per-week per-region for the term of the initial contract and revisit after Q1 of production. The 8-window suggestion is higher than we need initially.

Kira

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kira Johnson <kira@stratusai.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA discussion — regional latency carve-out

Kira — quick legal read:
- We'll accept a regional latency carve-out with explicit definitions for "burst windows" and incident detection. Please add a short clause in the redline listing the process for scheduling burst windows (email to account rep with at least 48 hours notice for recurring weekly windows; ad-hoc windows can be requested but subject to approval and bursts budget).
- Escalating credit schedule: Laura suggests combining Ben's proposed numerical bands with a clear cap and a dispute resolution timeline (30 days from notice).
- Auditability: we require Redwood to provide raw metrics (anonymized request counts + latency histograms) for disputed incidents. This can be provided via a shared dashboard link or CSV export with a signed NDA if needed.

I added a legal comment on page 3 of your PDF where the dispute notice and export requirements live.

-Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

1) Kira to confirm you want the incident detection window set to 5 or 10 minutes (reply by EOD Tuesday 5/11).
2) Alex to prepare a one-page summary of the burst-window scheduling process for the contract appendix.
3) Ben & Laura will produce the finalized redline and a capped credit table; target internal sign-off by 2027-05-13.

If you're comfortable with these milestones I'll prepare a short mutual action plan and send for signature.

Best,
Alex
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
